title: Choose the Moch mobile-first composition
question: Three full-page structures for the same friendly Moch brand. Pick the one the build should commit to; the selected wireframe becomes the spatial contract.

options.label: The Counter Recipe
options.thesis: Getting an agent on your phone feels like following a short, reassuring recipe.
options.viewport: Mobile: a large recipe-style hero card with the headline, Mochi, and two clear actions; below, a five-step vertical method and an ingredient strip for Linux, thinker and model. Desktop opens into a two-column counter with steps on the left and a live phone/runtime illustration on the right.
options.risk: Could feel too cute or domestic; the agent proof must stay concrete and the food metaphor must never become literal decoration.

options.label: The Pocket Field Guide
options.lineage: a pocket notebook and tabbed field guide
options.thesis: The site is a calm, trustworthy guide you keep in your pocket.
options.viewport: Mobile: a pocket-guide cover hero with Mochi peeking out, a bold headline and a download tab; a vertical tab rail leads through How it works, Choose your brain, What you can do and Local-first. Desktop becomes an open spread with guide notes on the left and real product UI on the right.
options.risk: Could become text-heavy or print-like on a phone; each tab needs a large product moment and very short notes.

options.label: The Playset
options.thesis: You build your own agent by snapping together a thinker, Linux and a model.
options.viewport: Mobile: the hero shows a phone-centered modular tray with Hermes/OpenCode, Linux and Model pieces; the headline and actions sit above and below. Scroll snaps through trays for Chat, Terminal and Browser. Desktop becomes a workbench with modules arranged around the phone.
options.risk: Could feel toy-like and weaken trust; the modules must contain realistic current UI, not abstract icons alone.
